findings.summary: The installed Skill entry is a fixed conformance macro rather than a complete per-owner-turn operation surface.
findings.evidence: application/graph_engineering/application/owner_turns.py requires the exact nine-operation tuple for every request, unconditionally creates a new task, and synthesizes discover, escalate, and result records instead of dispatching those operations through durable application/runtime paths. adapters/graph_engineering/adapters/owner_turn_local.py binds every external runtime port, including human request and presentation, to an unavailable stub. The isolated-wheel test performs one fresh all-in-one process and checks operation labels; it does not issue later separate same-lineage status/resume/escalate/result turns against the existing durable task. The production application also embeds artifact:prd-candidate, evidence:runtime-compatible, lease-plan:none, and a 1000000000 ns lease TTL instead of governed request/config data.
findings.required_change: Replace the fixed macro with a versioned per-owner-turn operation envelope that supports each of discover, create, clarify, approve, run, status, resume, escalate, and result independently. Later same-lineage turns must address an existing durable task and use real application/repository transitions plus exact presentation/result binding. Move PRD/evidence/lease references and lease TTL into validated governed request or configuration data; keep local fixture ports non-networked without placing fixture outcomes in production logic.
findings.verification: From an isolated installed wheel and both validated Skills, run separate process/turn invocations for create through interruption, then status, resume, escalation, and result against the same durable task for Codex, Hermes Telegram, and Hermes Discord. Assert exact durable revisions/events, result or presentation bindings and receipts, no background process, and nondisclosing zero-write rejection for foreign owner/runtime/lineage. Add static checks rejecting fixture constants, semantic references, and policy thresholds in production owner-turn logic.

findings.summary: Reviewer independence attestations can be replayed across different reviewer requests, tasks, runs, and candidates in the same session.
findings.evidence: core/graph_engineering/core/runtime.py ReviewerIndependenceAttestation binds author/reviewer/runtime/owner/lineage/session/capability/source but omits ReviewerRequest request_id, task_id, run_id, candidate_ref, candidate_digest, and request_digest. application/graph_engineering/application/runtime.py validates only that reduced tuple. An independent factory-attested adapter repro issued one attestation for review:A/task:A/candidate:A, replayed it for review:B/task:B/candidate:B in the same session, and both invoke_reviewer calls returned PASS. GEW-RT-039 covers same-identity rejection but not cross-request attestation replay.
findings.required_change: Bind the exact ReviewerRequest identity and digest into the self-digested independence attestation, including request, task, run, and candidate identity/digest, and compare the complete tuple before invoking the reviewer. A previously valid attestation must not authorize any other request or candidate.
findings.verification: Add factory-attested production-path tests for Codex, Hermes Telegram, and Hermes Discord that replay or substitute an attestation across request_id, task_id, run_id, candidate_ref, candidate_digest, and request_digest one field at a time. Every mutation must fail before the reviewer port call with zero writes; the exact matching fresh attestation and independently bound result must pass.
